body.statement:
Put \(a=1-\alpha\).  If \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), then
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge G_\alpha(\tau_n)
 =\begin{cases}
 2a-\dfrac{16}{3}\sqrt{\tau_n},
   &0\le\tau_n\le a^2/16,\\[6pt]
 \dfrac{a^3}{24\tau_n},&\tau_n>a^2/16.
 \end{cases}
\]
Moreover, there are constants \(c_{\mathrm{fix}}>0\) and
\(C_{\mathrm{low}}>0\), depending only on \(s\), \(M\), and
\(\alpha\), such that for every \(n\ge1\) and
\(0<\kappa_n\le1/8\),
\[
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)
 \ge c_{\mathrm{fix}}\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\},
 \qquad
 L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Fix any interval rule \(I_n\) satisfying the honesty constraint in
\(\text{def:minimax-length}\), and first suppose \(\kappa_n\le1/16\).
By \(\text{prop:moving-cutoff-membership-kl}\), every \(P_t\) belongs to
\(\mathcal P_n\), has effect label \(t\), and satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \le4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}.
\]
Honesty under \(P_t\) and the defining variational inequality for total
variation therefore imply, for every \(t\in[-1,1]\),
\[
 P_0^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}
 \ge P_t^{\otimes n}\{t\in I_n\}
     -\operatorname{TV}(P_t^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \ge1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}.
\]
The left side is nonnegative.  To justify the coverage integration
without any unrecorded interchange theorem, fix \(m\ge1\) and use the
equally spaced grid \(t_j=-1+2j/m\), \(j=0,\ldots,m\).  For every
connected \(I_n\subset[-1,1]\), the number of grid points in \(I_n\)
is at most \(1+m|I_n|/2\).  Hence, deterministically,
\[
 |I_n|\ge\frac2m\sum_{j=0}^m\mathbf 1\{t_j\in I_n\}-\frac2m.
\]
Taking expectations uses only linearity for this finite sum.  Applying
the preceding probability bound and then letting \(m\to\infty\), the
Riemann sums converge because
\(t\mapsto[1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_n|t|}]_+\) is continuous.  Therefore
\[
 E_{P_0}|I_n|
 \ge2\int_0^1[1-\alpha-4\sqrt{\tau_nt}]_+\,dt
 =G_\alpha(\tau_n).
\]
Because \(P_0\in\mathcal P_n\), the worst-case expected length of every
honest rule is at least this quantity; taking the infimum over such rules
proves the first inequality.

To evaluate the integral, write \(a=1-\alpha\).  If
\(\tau_n\le a^2/16\), its integrand is positive throughout \([0,1]\),
and
\[
 2\int_0^1(a-4\sqrt{\tau_nt})\,dt
 =2a-\frac{16}{3}\sqrt{\tau_n}.
\]
If \(\tau_n>a^2/16\), the positive region ends at
\(t_0=a^2/(16\tau_n)\), and
\[
 2\int_0^{t_0}(a-4\sqrt{\tau_nt})\,dt
 =2\left(at_0-\frac83\sqrt{\tau_n}t_0^{3/2}\right)
 =\frac{a^3}{24\tau_n}.
\]
This proves the closed form in \(\text{def:integrated-slope-lower-function}\).

We next use the fixed-cutoff family.  Let
\[
 p_s=2+\frac1s,
 \qquad
 C_b=2\left(\frac{4H_s}{M}\right)^{1/s},
 \qquad
 \gamma=\min\left\{1,
 \left(\frac{(1-2\alpha)^2}{16C_b}\right)^{1/p_s}\right\},
\]
and choose the positive label
\[
 u_n=\gamma\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}.
\]
Since \(\rho_n=n^{-s/(2s+1)}\), one has
\(n\rho_n^{p_s}=1\).  If \(\rho_n\le\kappa_n\), then
\(n(\kappa_nu_n)^{p_s}=\gamma^{p_s}\); if
\(\rho_n>\kappa_n\), the left side is at most
\(\gamma^{p_s}n\rho_n^{p_s}=\gamma^{p_s}\).  The preceding proposition
therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{u_n}^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le\sqrt{C_b\gamma^{p_s}}
 \le\frac{1-2\alpha}{4}.
\]
Both laws are in \(\mathcal P_n\).  Honesty and total variation imply
under \(Q_0\)
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_0^{\otimes n}\{0,u_n\in I_n\}
 &\ge1-Q_0^{\otimes n}\{0\notin I_n\}
       -Q_0^{\otimes n}\{u_n\notin I_n\}\\
 &\ge1-2\alpha-
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{u_n}^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \ge\frac34(1-2\alpha).
 \end{aligned}
\]
On this event, connectedness of \(I_n\subset[-1,1]\) forces
\(|I_n|\ge u_n\).  Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n|
 \ge E_{Q_0}|I_n|
 \ge \frac34(1-2\alpha)\gamma
       \min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}.
\]
Taking the infimum proves the fixed-cutoff inequality with
\(c_{\mathrm{fix}}=3(1-2\alpha)\gamma/4>0\).

It remains to combine the two lower bounds.  The displayed formula for
\(G_\alpha\) implies, for every \(\tau>0\),
\[
 G_\alpha(\tau)
 \ge \frac{(1-\alpha)^3}{24}\min\{1,\tau^{-1}\}.
\]
Indeed, below the breakpoint its minimum is
\(2(1-\alpha)/3\), between the breakpoint and one the second branch is
at least \((1-\alpha)^3/24\), and above one the second branch equals
\((1-\alpha)^3/(24\tau)\).  Thus, when \(\kappa_n\le1/16\), the maximum
of the moving- and fixed-cutoff lower bounds is at least a positive
constant times
\[
 \min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}
 +\min\left\{1,\frac1{n\kappa_n^3}\right\}
 \ge
 \min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}
                 +\frac1{n\kappa_n^3}\right\}
 =r_n.
\]
When \(\kappa_n>1/16\), the location term is already absorbed by the
fixed-cutoff term, because
\[
 \frac{1}{n\kappa_n^3}
 \le256\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n},
\]
where \(n\rho_n=n^{(s+1)/(2s+1)}\ge1\) was used.  Hence
\(r_n\le257\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}\), and the fixed-cutoff inequality
again yields \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\ge C_{\mathrm{low}}r_n\) after reducing
the constant.  This proves the all-strength lower frontier.
body.justification: The two legal causal continua isolate the location-slope and fixed-cutoff nonparametric sources of difficulty and combine to prove the complete lower half of the candidate all-strength frontier.
body.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy procedures do not supply the moving-location term, while sharp unknown-cutoff rates do not supply the weak causal-ratio term; the theorem derives both within one unchanged full model.
body.consumer: An analyst obtains a design-independent impossibility benchmark: no honest connected interval can beat \(r_n\), even before the proposed profile procedure is shown to attain it.
